sections.h2: Where is Tuscaloosa, Alabama, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Tuscaloosa is the county seat of Tuscaloosa County in west-central Alabama, on the Black Warrior River at the point where the Gulf Coastal and Piedmont plains meet. It sits about 60 miles southwest of Birmingham.

The city covers 72.22 square miles, but only 62.15 of that is land. The other 10.07 square miles is water, most of it Lake Tuscaloosa (which lies entirely inside the city limits) and the river itself. The terrain shifts from forested hills in the northeast to a low, marshy plain in the southwest, so the ground under a house can differ a lot from one side of town to the other.

Wikipedia's city article lists these major areas of the city proper:

  • Downtown Tuscaloosa and Central or Midtown Tuscaloosa
  • The University of Alabama main campus
  • Alberta and Hillcrest
  • East Tuscaloosa and West Tuscaloosa
  • North River, along the lake and river corridor

A seller in Alberta deals with a different set of buyers than a seller beside the campus, so it helps to know which of these areas your street belongs to before you talk price with anyone.

sections.h2: What is the history of Tuscaloosa, and why does it matter to a seller?
sections.html:
The territorial legislature incorporated Tuscaloosa on December 13, 1819, one day before Congress admitted Alabama as a state. The town served as the state capital from 1826 to 1846, and the University of Alabama opened here in 1831.

That history left a layered housing stock. The city is nicknamed the Druid City for the water oaks planted along its downtown streets starting in the 1840s, and the 1850s brought the state hospital now known as Bryce Hospital. Locks and dams built on the Black Warrior River in the 1890s linked the town by water to the port of Mobile, which helped mining and metal industries take hold.

For a seller, age is the practical point. An older house near downtown may have dated plumbing, old wiring or a roof that was patched more than once, and those items often decide whether a financed buyer's inspection goes smoothly or falls apart.

sections.h2: How big is Tuscaloosa and how fast is it growing?
sections.html:
Tuscaloosa is Alabama's fifth most populous city, with 99,600 residents at the 2020 census and a Census Bureau estimate above 114,000 for July 1, 2025. The 2020 count was a 10.1 percent rise over 2010.

MeasureFigure
Population, 2010 census90,468
Population, 2020 census99,600
Households, 202040,817
Median age, 202027.1 years
Total area72.22 square miles
Elevation190 feet

A median age of 27.1 is young for any American city, and it reflects how many students live here. The metropolitan area also includes Hale and Pickens counties, so the buyer pool for a Tuscaloosa house is a regional one.

sections.h2: What jobs drive the Tuscaloosa housing market?
sections.html:
The University of Alabama is the city's largest employer, and Wikipedia credits it with more than $2.5 billion in yearly economic impact. Mercedes-Benz U.S. International is the biggest industrial name, with more than 6,100 employees and over 11,000 further jobs supported through regional suppliers.

Other employers named for the area include:

  • Parts suppliers such as Brose Tuscaloosa, ARD Logistics and ZF Chassis Systems
  • JVC America, Nucor Steel, BFGoodrich Tire Manufacturing and Hunt Refining
  • GAF Materials, gChem and The Westervelt Company, which has its headquarters here
  • Federal research sites on campus, including a U.S. Geological Survey facility and the National Water Center

Retail clusters around 15th Street and McFarland Boulevard, including The Shoppes at Legacy Park and University Mall, add to the job base. Owners of rentals near campus often have leases and tenant turnover to sort out before a sale.

sections.h2: What should a Tuscaloosa homeowner know about tornadoes and storm damage?
sections.html:
Tuscaloosa has a documented record of violent tornadoes, and any house here can carry a storm history. Wikipedia's climate section notes that severe thunderstorms bring damaging winds, large hail and occasionally tornadoes.

DateEvent
January 1997F2 tornado, one death
December 2000F4 tornado in Tuscaloosa County, eleven deaths
April 15, 2011EF3 tornado
April 27, 2011EF4 tornado, about 1.5 miles wide, estimated 190 mph winds, 44 deaths in the city

The April 27 storm caused an estimated $2.45 billion in damage. It is the reference point for every storm conversation in town, so buyers and insurers ask about roof age, hail claims and any repairs after a storm.

If your house took hail or wind damage and the repair never happened, a financed buyer may be unable to close until it is fixed. A buyer who pays cash and takes the house as it stands removes that hurdle, though you should still disclose what you know.

sections.h2: What is the climate in Tuscaloosa and how does it affect a house?
sections.html:
Tuscaloosa has a humid subtropical climate, with a July daily average of 81.7 degrees Fahrenheit and 71 to 72 days a year at 90 degrees or higher. January averages 44.7 degrees, and the temperature drops to freezing or below on about 46 days a year.

That mix puts steady work on air conditioning, attic insulation and roofing in summer. Rain is abundant, with January and February the wettest months, while snow averages only 0.7 inches a season. Wet winters are hard on crawl spaces, gutters and old siding, and buyers' inspectors look for moisture first.

sections.h2: How do schools, roads and transit shape where people want to live in Tuscaloosa?
sections.html:
Higher education is a major draw. The University of Alabama, Stillman College and Shelton State Community College are all based in the city, and each has a library open to the public.

The Tuscaloosa Public Library is a joint city and county agency with three branches. School district lines in the county are set by the districts, so confirm which system serves your address before you describe it to a buyer. The school offices can give you a firm answer for a specific street.

The city lies about 60 miles southwest of Birmingham, and the metro area spans Tuscaloosa, Hale and Pickens counties.

sections.h2: What taxes and fees apply when a Tuscaloosa house is sold?
sections.html:
Alabama charges a recordation tax on a deed, and the formula in Alabama Code section 40-22-1 is 50 cents for each $500 of value or fraction of $500. On a $160,000 sale the arithmetic is 320 units of $500 at 50 cents, which comes to $160 before the recording fee and before any mortgage adjustment the statute allows.

The probate judge calculates that tax when the deed is presented. A deed should come with proof of the actual purchase price, using a form developed by the Alabama Department of Revenue.

The Alabama Department of Revenue says property tax is due October 1 and becomes delinquent after December 31. If a sale closes late in the year, ask the Tuscaloosa County tax office for the current balance and any unpaid prior years. Call that office before closing day, because its payoff steps may differ from what we describe here.

  • Request the current tax figure early.
  • Collect lien payoffs for any mortgage, judgment or code fine.
  • Sign the deed in front of a notary, as the closing agent directs.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale fit a Tuscaloosa owner?
sections.html:
A cash sale fits when speed or condition matters more to you than the last few thousand dollars a full repair and listing might bring. In Tuscaloosa that usually means one of these situations:

  • A student rental that needs paint, flooring and cleaning after a lease ends.
  • An inherited house that relatives cannot agree on or do not want to maintain.
  • A property with storm or roof damage that a lender's appraiser would flag.
  • An owner who must relocate for a job.

We buy houses in Tuscaloosa as they are, and you decide whether to accept what we offer. It costs nothing to ask, and you can compare our number with a listing agent's before you choose.

faqs.q: What county is Tuscaloosa, Alabama, in?
faqs.a: Tuscaloosa is in Tuscaloosa County, and it is the county seat. The city lies on the Black Warrior River in west-central Alabama.

faqs.q: Was Tuscaloosa ever the capital of Alabama?
faqs.a: Yes. Tuscaloosa was the state capital from 1826 to 1846, before the capital moved to Montgomery.

faqs.q: How are property taxes due in Tuscaloosa?
faqs.a: Alabama property taxes are due October 1 and delinquent after December 31, according to the Alabama Department of Revenue. Contact the Tuscaloosa County tax office for your balance.

faqs.q: How much is the deed tax on a Tuscaloosa sale?
faqs.a: State law sets it at 50 cents per $500 of value, so a $200,000 house works out to $200 before fees. The probate judge collects it when the deed is recorded.

faqs.q: Does the 2011 tornado still matter when selling?
faqs.a: It can. Buyers and insurers often ask about storm damage, roof age and repairs, so keep records of any work done on the house.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Tuscaloosa house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. A buyer who pays cash can take a house in its current condition, and we buy Tuscaloosa houses as they are.
